messages.subject: Version 1.2.5 released
messages.body_plain:
The version 1.2.5 of the Vim-R-plugin was released:

> http://www.vim.org/scripts/script.php?script_id=2628

The changes are:
New command to evaluate selection and get output in newtab: \so
The command \ao no longer blocks Vim.
New command (\rv) and new options (vimrplugin_csv_warn, vimrplugin_csv_app and vimrplugin_df_viewer).
Bring back the "echo" send commands because some users need them.
It is also necessary to install a new version of the vimcom package:

> http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/vimcom.html

messages.subject: RStart to start R session in a vim commandline argument?
messages.subject_clean: RStart to start R session in a vim commandline argument?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I am new to Vim-R-plugin and still a novice in Vim. Is it possible to do something like this?

vim -c "call RStart" myscript.R

from my search, it think it is possible to do so with vim's autocmd. But I don't want to mess with that yet, partly because I don't know how to make the call only applied for R filetype. Therefore I prefer a solution to run from commandline argument.

messages.subject: Re: RStart to start R session in a vim commandline argument?
messages.subject_clean: RStart to start R session in a vim commandline argument?
messages.body_plain:
You can do:

vim --servername VIM -c "call StartR('R')" myscript.R

If you are going to this often, you might want to put in your .bashrc:

alias vimr="vim --servername VIM -c 'call StartR(\"R\")'"

Then you can do:

vimr myscript.R
